getSamples

getSamples.Rd

Function that gets samples, either from a regular bootstrap (PsN output), a SIR (PsN output), or a covariance matrix (NONMEM output). It includes protective coding to ensure the parameter estimates in the .ext data align with the dimensions of the .cov matrix.

Usage

getSamples(
  input,
  extFile = NULL,
  n = NULL,
  indexvec = NULL,
  zerosindex = NULL,
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

input

The input file name (character string). If the file name extension is .cov it is assumed that the file is a NONMEM .cov file. If the extension is .csv, it is assumed to be a PsN raw results file from a bootstrap or SIR. Can also be a numeric data.frame containing only parameter estimates; in this case, the user is responsible for column naming and subsetting.

extFile

The name of the NONMEM .ext file (character string) OR a data.frame containing the parameter iterations. Providing a data.frame allows for manual alignment or "padding" of parameters if NONMEM has omitted columns in the .cov file.

n

The number of samples to generate when sampling from a variance-covariance matrix. This is required if input is a .cov file. NULL is permissible if the input is a SIR or bootstrap raw_results file.

indexvec

A vector used to subset columns in the raw results file so parameters appear in the order: THETA, SIGMA, OMEGA. Not required if a PsN raw_results_structure file is in the same directory.

zerosindex

A vector of indices indicating which parameters are fixed to zero.

quiet

If FALSE (default), an informational message is printed when a SIR raw_results file is detected (and when n is ignored for such a file). Set to TRUE to silence these messages.

Value

A data frame with $n + 1$ rows (if $n$ is specified for file inputs) or the full set of resamples. The first row contains the final parameter estimates (ITERATION -1000000000), followed by the samples. For a SIR raw_results file the samples are the importance-resampled parameter vectors (resamples == 1), again with the final estimates prepended as the first row. Note: If input is a data.frame, the function returns exactly $n$ samples (if $n$ is specified) or the exact input data.frame (if $n$ is NULL), without appending a row of base estimates.

Details

Protective Coding: When sampling from a .cov file, the function verifies that the number of parameters in the extFile matches the dimensions of the covariance matrix. If a mismatch is detected (a known NONMEM edge case), the function will stop() and prompt the user to provide a manually aligned data.frame to extFile.

See also

vignette("Part2-walkthrough", package = "PMXForest") for how this fits the whole workflow.

Examples

covFile <- system.file("extdata", "SimVal/run7.cov", package = "PMXForest")
extFile <- system.file("extdata", "SimVal/run7.ext", package = "PMXForest")
bootFile <- system.file("extdata", "SimVal/bs7.dir/raw_results_run7bs.csv",
  package = "PMXForest"
)
sirFile <- system.file("extdata", "SimVal/sir7.dir/raw_results_run7.csv",
  package = "PMXForest"
)

# Covariance matrix: n draws from the implied multivariate normal
mySamplesCov <- getSamples(covFile, extFile, n = 50)

# Non-parametric bootstrap: the resamples themselves
mySamplesBS <- getSamples(bootFile, extFile)

# "Small bootstrap": build a covariance matrix from the resamples, draw n from it
mySamplesSmallBS <- getSamples(bootFile, extFile, n = 50)

# SIR
mySamplesSir <- getSamples(sirFile, extFile)
#> SIR raw_results detected: using the 1000 importance-resampled parameter vectors (resamples == 1).

# A plain numeric data frame of parameter vectors is also a valid input
dfParameters <- getSamples(bootFile, extFile)
getSamples(dfParameters) # use the rows as-is
